{{Short description|Statistical method}}
[[Survival analysis]] is normally carried out using [[parametric model]]s, [[Semiparametric model|semi-parametric models]], [[non-parametric model]]s to estimate the [[survival rate]] in clinical research. However recently Bayesian models<ref>{{Cite book|title=Bayesian Survival Analysis – Springer|last=Ibrahim|first=Joseph G.|last2=Chen|first2=Ming-Hui|last3=Sinha|first3=Debajyoti|doi=10.1007/978-1-4757-3447-8|series = Springer Series in Statistics|year = 2001|isbn = 978-1-4419-2933-4}}</ref> are also used to estimate the [[survival rate]] due to their ability to handle design and analysis issues in clinical research.<ref name="Sinha1997">{{cite journal|last1=Sinha|first1=Debajyoti|authorlink2=Dipak K. Dey|last2=Dey|first2=Dipak K.|title=Semiparametric Bayesian Analysis of Survival Data|journal=Journal of the American Statistical Association|date=September 1997|volume=92|issue=439|pages=1195–1212|doi=10.1080/01621459.1997.10474077}}</ref>
